subject.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)

question: Should public `cron run` permanently be a fully non-consuming operator action for all cron schedules and outcomes, with scheduler state owned only by timer and on-exit watcher execution?
rationale: The branch intentionally changes retry, backoff, next-run, and terminal-state ownership beyond the reported one-shot deletion bug; code review cannot choose that durable product contract without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
options.body: Keep the internal origin split and document that public manual runs record outcomes without consuming or modifying scheduler-owned state.

options.title: Narrow the scope
options.body: Preserve only the one-shot protection and retain selected scheduler effects for manual runs if that is the intended operator contract.

recommendation.title: Adopt non-consuming operator runs
recommendation.body: Keep the internal origin split and document that public manual runs record outcomes without consuming or modifying scheduler-owned state.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged cron scheduling work owns the closely related due-slot and recomputation invariants affected by this contract choice.
